summary: F15 currency race + refund/chargeback clawback + secret rotation ALL verified end-to-end. Focused suites: tests/test_currency_race_and_refunds.py 20/20 PASS and tests/test_no_committed_secrets.py 8/8 PASS (28/28 in a single -o addopts='' -q run, 3.43s). Independent race verification (/tmp/independent_race.py): fresh account, 8 concurrent /api/pay/order calls mixing region=IN and region=US+currency=USD — result: ONE wallet doc, currency locked to INR by the first winner, every 200 response's currency == INR, the 4 USD requests were correctly refused with the INR-pack message ('Choose one of the top-up packs: 99, 199, 499'), all 4 payment links cancelled via LIVE Razorpay API — the race is now serialized. Independent secret scan: grep against every git-TRACKED file for <redacted>, <redacted>, <redacted> and <redacted> returned NO hits; git ls-files backend/.env frontend/.env is empty. Damage control confirmed by unit tests: credit_wallet_once with a wallet-vs-payment currency mismatch credits NOTHING, sets status='currency_mismatch' + needs_review=true, and writes no ledger row; the ledger row now carries the currency actually paid (99.0 INR, not hardcoded USD). Razorpay refund clawback exercised via HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks: full refund zeroes balance and writes a -99.0 INR row keyed 'refund:<id>' with kind='clawback' and shortfall=0, partial refund debits 49 and flips status to 'partially_refunded', refund.created→refund.processed for the same id claws back exactly once (second is duplicate=true, clawed_back=false, count==1), a refund of 99 against a wallet with only 10 caps recovery at 10 and records shortfall=89 with balance floored at 0 (never negative), refund for unknown payment returns ignored='unknown payment' and touches nothing, currency-mismatched refund returns ignored='refund currency mismatch', payment.dispute.lost claws back the full 99 and sets status='chargeback', unsigned refund POST returns 400 and balance unchanged. Apple/RevenueCat: iap.classify_event maps CANCELLATION and REFUND for our consumables to 'clawback', UNSUBSCRIBE is ignored, CANCELLATION for a product we never sold is ignored, NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE is still 'credit'; the LIVE POST /api/pay/iap/webhook path (with REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_AUTH) claws back exactly what our own wallet_ledger recorded (-99.0 for the seeded txn) and a CANCELLATION with no prior credit returns ignored='no credit on record for this transaction'. Full backend regression: 603 passed / 9 skipped in 248.27s — matches the review-request baseline exactly. Frontend smoke (mobile 390x844): AUTH_DEBUG_RETURN_OTP=true temporarily, email OTP sign-in with a fresh iter22-<hex>@example.com — DEV MODE code read from screen, consent accepted, Analyze tab renders (trending/stocks/crypto/commodities + $0.00 chip), AGENTS tab renders the wallet card with the $0.00 balance chip and $5/$10/$25 top-up packs (USD, correct for a non-+91 account), account-identity == the signed-in email. No red screen, no console errors. env restored to AUTH_DEBUG_RETURN_OTP=false, backend restarted, verified on disk; smoke seed data cleaned (1 user / 3 wallets / 1 otp_requests / 20 stray free_credit_grants). One FRONTEND blocker discovered en route and fixed: /app/frontend/src/components/LightweightChart.tsx line 71 embedded literal backticks (`openssl dgst -sha384`) inside a JS template literal, which closed the string early and made Metro fail with 'SyntaxError: Missing semicolon (71:52)' — the web bundle was returning 500 for the entire app. Removed the two stray backticks in the HTML comment; the SRI hash on line 78 and its intent are untouched. Expo restarted, / returns 200, bundle loads. Deprecated packages / SafeAreaView / other RN issues: none observed.
action_items: Consider adding a lint/CI guard that flags stray backticks inside JS template literals in *.tsx (or splitting LightweightChart.tsx's HTML template into a plain .html asset or a String.raw block) — the F15 fix landed correctly but the concurrent chart-SRI pin shipped with a syntax bug that took the whole web preview offline, and neither pytest nor tsc catches it because it's a bundler-time error.
Rotate the OLD Razorpay TEST key that git HISTORY still contains (documented, expected — flagged only so it isn't forgotten).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/payments.credit_wallet_once now guards on the wallet's LOCKED currency BEFORE the $inc, so even if the /pay/order race somehow slipped, the money guard on the credit path is a second, independent safety. The ledger row now writes the currency actually paid (line ~192) instead of hardcoded USD — visible in test_ledger_records_the_currency_actually_paid.

routes/payments.claw_back_once uses conditional_debit + shortfall math with a floor at 0 (balance never goes negative even when refund > current balance) and stores `requested`, `recovered`, `shortfall` on the ledger row so an operator can see exactly what the customer walked away with. The `payment_id` key `refund:<id>` / `chargeback:<pid>` gives idempotency across refund.created↔refund.processed and across duplicate dispute events.

routes/payments.handle_refund_event refuses cross-currency refunds (ignored='refund currency mismatch') and unknown payments (ignored='unknown payment') — neither can move money. The unsigned-webhook 400 path is untouched by the refund/dispute branch, so signature bypass isn't possible via a refund event.

iap.classify_event returns 'clawback' for the true refund/cancellation types and 'ignore' for UNSUBSCRIBE and for non-consumable product_ids — the Apple side reverses what OUR ledger row recorded, not the current price table, which is the only honest amount to give back.

tests/test_no_committed_secrets.py has NOT_SECRET explicitly listing REVENUECAT_IOS_KEY (public SDK key, safe to ship) but scans everything else in .env by real-value equality, plus the shape scan for rzp_ / sk-emergent- / AC / SK / sk- — this is stronger than a regex-only scan and would immediately catch a paste like the iteration_15 incident.

One concurrent regression: /app/frontend/src/components/LightweightChart.tsx line 71 had literal backticks inside a JS template literal — fixed in this iteration. Root cause was the SRI-pin comment; the SRI hash itself is fine.

rca_of_issue: F15 (currency race): before this pass, /pay/order picked currency from the request every time and set it on the wallet unconditionally — two simultaneous first top-ups from opposite regions both saw balance=0 and currency=None, both wrote their own currency, and whichever landed second silently overwrote the first. The link the app opened for the losing race was payable into a wallet that now spoke a different language — ₹99 could add 99 to a USD wallet. Fix (verified): the write is now a Mongo find_one_and_update({device_id: key, currency: {$in: [null, '']}}, {$set: {currency: desired}}, return_document=AFTER) — the FIRST claim wins atomically, every subsequent /pay/order (including the concurrent ones in test_parallel_claims_produce_exactly_one_currency and the real 8-way race in /tmp/independent_race.py) sees currency!=null and adopts the locked value; credit_wallet_once then refuses any payment whose currency ≠ wallet.currency and flags it needs_review instead of crediting. Refund clawback: previously a refund left the credit on the balance because the webhook only handled payment.captured — the refund/refund.processed/refund.created/payment.dispute.lost paths now go through handle_refund_event → claw_back_once, keyed by refund:<id>/chargeback:<pid> for idempotency, with a shortfall column and a hard floor at 0 so a refund can never drive the wallet negative. Secret rotation: no tracked file contains any of the 4 flagged tokens, backend/.env is untracked (git ls-files returns empty), REVENUECAT_IOS_KEY is intentionally listed as public in NOT_SECRET (RevenueCat iOS keys are shipped in the client). The bundler-time SyntaxError in LightweightChart.tsx was the concurrent chart-SRI-pin change from the interim iteration mentioned in the review request (line 71 embedded literal backticks inside a JS template literal) — fixed here.
